reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is a step-by-step educational demonstration of creating and operating a Solana meme coin, explicitly framed as not financial advice. The wallet approvals, bot configuration, liquidity removal, and earnings claims are presented as a demonstrated process and claimed result, without establishing deceptive viewer solicitation, a completed transfer, victim loss, or a verified outcome.

citations.quote: In this step-by-step video, we show how to build and deploy your own meme coin on Solana using AMM FORGE— no scripts, no experience required.
Launch your memecoin here - https://www.ammforge.com/ Promote memecoin via bot here: https://bot.ammforge.com/
this content is strictly for educational purposes, not financial advice.
now just approve the transaction in your wallet and you are all set.

opening.argument: The video does more than describe trading mechanics: it links activating and funding a volume bot to immediate visibility, buyers, and extraordinary income. Viewers are directed to use the promoted service, choose a budget, configure buying pressure, and approve a wallet transaction, while the speaker says the bot brings in buyers and presents the process as the route to $36,000-per-launch earnings. That is a direct solicitation structure: take the requested wallet and bot actions, then expect the promoted trading operation to produce returns.

citations.quote: amforge.com lets you promote your coin instantel with a built-in volume bot right after launch
Set the budget, I set the total sole budget for. Believe me, this 4 SOL is worth it.
This is what boosts your coins visibility and brings in early buyers instantly
This is exactly how I'm making $36k per meme coin launch every single day.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the presentation educational does not remove the action-and-reward linkage. The disclaimer is only a characterization of the content, while the actual instructions direct viewers to a specific service, wallet approvals, a funded bot, and liquidity removal. The described process therefore operates as a solicitation even if the video does not document a viewer's completed loss.

citations.quote: this content is strictly for educational purposes, not financial advice.
Launch your memecoin here - https://www.ammforge.com/ Promote memecoin via bot here: https://bot.ammforge.com/
select your pool, slide it to 100%, click remove 100% liquidity

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those instructions show a demonstration of actions, not a promise that viewers will receive the speaker's claimed result. The service is described as a tool for promotion, and the earnings statement is a speaker claim; neither establishes that a viewer must transfer funds to the speaker or that the outcome is guaranteed. Wallet approval alone does not show deceptive acquisition of viewer assets.

citations.quote: In this step-by-step video, we show how to build and deploy your own meme coin on Solana using AMM FORGE— no scripts, no experience required.
this content is strictly for educational purposes, not financial advice.
436 SOL earned, that's insane, absolutely unreal!

opening.argument: The risk signals reinforce one another rather than appearing as isolated technical details. The video shows a wallet approval beside token forging, then a volume-bot configuration with a 4 SOL budget and 80% buying pressure, and finally displays a claimed 436 SOL return. The speaker also calls the process fast and says it is producing buyers and $36,000 every day. A crypto bot funded through wallet approval and paired with unusually large, easy-looking returns is presented as a repeatable path, while the evidence does not substantiate the promised economics.

citations.quote: Switch the frequency to fast. Set buying pressure to 80% Now go ahead and click Launch volume bot Approve the transaction
This is exactly how I'm making $36k per meme coin launch every single day.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The disclaimer and demonstration framing cannot neutralize the combination of fast execution, wallet authorization, bot funding, automated buying pressure, and a claimed hundreds-of-SOL return. The issue is not whether one screenshot independently proves fraud; it is that the video uses the sequence to make a high-risk, highly profitable workflow look routine and repeatable.

citations.quote: this content is strictly for educational purposes, not financial advice.
The token creation process has officially started, the fee is super low, almost nothing
436 SOL earned, that's insane, absolutely unreal!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are visible interface states and narrated claims, not independent proof of a return or a guarantee to viewers. The frame showing a transaction approval does not establish what was ultimately transferred, and the earnings display does not establish that the amount was realized or reproducible. Risky or unusual crypto mechanics alone do not prove deceptive intent.

citations.quote: Whether you're running an experiment, simulating a soft rug, or just exploring crypto mechanics — this walkthrough is made for you.

opening.argument: The educational wrapper functions as promotion because nearly every substantive step steers viewers to named commercial destinations and participation. The description supplies one destination to launch a coin and another to promote it with a bot, while the narration praises the service as quick, easy, and superior to alternatives. The walkthrough then demonstrates wallet connection, token creation, bot configuration, and liquidity removal, ending with a recurring-income claim. This is operational marketing for a bot-assisted crypto launch, not neutral explanation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presence of a disclaimer does not change the video's practical effect. It identifies a named platform, tells viewers where to go, explains how to connect a wallet and fund the bot, and praises the resulting performance. Describing those steps as a walkthrough does not account for the repeated destination links and promotional language.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A tutorial may legitimately name the tools needed to reproduce a technical demonstration. The description expressly frames the material as a walkthrough and even mentions experimenting or simulating a soft rug, which is consistent with explaining mechanics rather than promising viewers a payout. Praise and links do not establish that the platform solicited a deceptive transfer or that the displayed result was verified.
